description:
PearCal is a peer-to-peer calendar app that syncs directly between devices — no server, no cloud, no accounts required.

Your calendar data never leaves your group. It lives only on the devices of the people you choose to share with, powered by Hypercore Protocol.

FEATURES

Peer Groups

Create a group and invite others via a share link or QR code. Each group has its own color and avatar. Members see only the events shared with them.

Events & Reminders

Create one-time or recurring events. Set a reminder time per event. Selectively share events with specific group members — not everyone in a group has to see every event.

Holidays
Optional US, Canada, and UK public holiday calendars. Toggle per country from your profile. Holiday events are read-only and stored locally only.

Privacy First

No account creation. No email address. No tracking. No ads. Your data stays on your devices.

Open Source
PearCal is free and open source. Source code is available on GitHub.

PERMISSIONS

Camera — used to set your profile photo and scan QR invite codes.
Photo Library — used to set your profile photo.
whatsNew:
## What's Changed

### Improvements

  - Mexican holidays: Turn on Mexico in Settings > Holidays and your calendar fills in the seven national rest days, plus election day and the presidential
  handover in the years they fall. The three holidays that move to a Monday move on their own.

### Bug Fixes

  - The home-screen widget shows today again: Overnight it kept yesterday's events under today's date, and opening the app once did not always fix it. It
  now turns the page at midnight on its own, and keeps a week of days ready so it is never showing the wrong one.
  - Blind peers on Start9 start up again: After the StartOS 0.4 update, a blind peer would fail to start and keep restarting because the update moved its
  data folder. It now repairs itself and carries on.
  - Installing a blind peer on Start9 0.4 works: Install and update were failing with a not-found error. The right package is now published for 0.4 boxes.
